content.text: The verifier's four substantive bullets all affirm the finding — classification, cited text, output shape, and rationale — and expressly label the failing deterministic check a false signal. There is no defect to repair, so I am resubmitting the same compliant finding without substantive change rather than manufacturing an edit to satisfy an inapplicable check.

input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale: Compliant; no redline. The Agreement grants Kubient no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right over AP. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verif" return no hits, and a full read of the Agreement (p0000-p0074) confirms no such right. The only access-flavoured language is Section 1 (p0001), where AP agrees to provide "reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services" — a service-enablement cooperation covenant, not a right to examine AP's books, usage or systems, and containing no remote or system-access grant that would reach walk-away territory. Direction: this rule caps a Vendor-favourable right, so its complete absence is more favourable to AP than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access). There is nothing to limit, and inserting audit parameters would create a Vendor right we do not currently face. "Missing" would also be wrong: the rule constrains a Vendor right rather than procuring an entitlement for us. This fits the commercial bargain, since fees flow from Kubient to AP under a revenue share with sequential liability (Section 5, p0023), leaving no AP usage or underpayment to audit. The deterministic "audit frequency limited" check fails only because no audit clause exists to carry a frequency cap; it is a false signal, not evidence of unlimited or unannounced audits. Residual internal note: Exhibits are incorporated under Section 1, so if any Exhibit or amendment later introduces audit or system-access language, we should require the preferred parameters at that time.
